_note: Excerpts copied from the alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text (PDF extraction) read on 2026-10-25 by the paper-stage agent. PDF extraction splits sub/superscripts onto separate lines; the prose of each excerpt is as extracted, with fractions, sub/superscripts and Greek letters rejoined linearly and elisions marked '...'. Durable references are the arXiv version identifiers and page numbers given with each excerpt. These are prose and displayed-equation excerpts (not theorem statements), so tools/citation_check.py, which accepts only theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary excerpts, was NOT run on them.

ku_rates.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, Fixation probability in Moran-like Processes on graphs, arXiv:2403.12598v2 [math.PR], 11 Sep 2024, p. 2 (Section 1.1, eq. (3))
ku_rates.text: We denote with p+(j) the probability to increase the mutant population by one, assuming j mutants present in the population. Analogously, for the probability to decrease the mutant population by one, which we denote with p-(j). We thus denote p+(j) := r/(1 + (r-1) j/n) * (j/n) (n-j)/n, p-(j) := 1/(1 + (r-1) j/n) * ((n-j)/n) (j/n), (3) where j is the current number of mutants in the population. The states 0 and n are absorbing. ... The individual to be replaced is chosen uniformly at random.

ku_fix.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, arXiv:2403.12598v2, pp. 3-4 (Sections 1.1.2-1.1.3, eq. (4))
ku_fix.text: For r != 1, one notices that equations (1),(2) fulfil for every j, 0 < j < n, p-/p+ = 1/r. Furthermore, the function h(j) := r^{-j} is harmonic on the transient states {1, 2, ..., n-1} and thus (r^{-M_k})_{k>=0} is a martingale, too. The Optional Stopping Theorem then implies ... P(T_fix < infinity | M_0 = i) = (1 - 1/r^i)/(1 - 1/r^n). [p. 3] ... the absorption probabilities rho_i := i/n for r = 1 and (1 - 1/r^i)/(1 - 1/r^n) for r != 1, i in {1, 2, ..., n-1}, (4) are referred to as Moran fixation probabilities. [p. 4]

ku_typos.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, arXiv:2403.12598v2, pp. 2, 3 and 7
ku_typos.text: p. 2, Section 1.1.1 'Symmetric case r = 1 (neutral selection)': 'For r = 0 the equations (1) and (2) simplify for all j, 0 < j < n, to p+(j) = (j/n)((n-j)/n) = p-(j).' [typo in the source: r = 1 is meant]. p. 3, Section 1.1.2: right after 'the function h(j) := r^{-j} is harmonic ... thus (r^{-M_k}) is a martingale', the optional-stopping line is printed (pdftotext of the arXiv PDF, exponents flattened) as 'ri = E[rM0] = E[rMT] = (1 - P(T_fix < inf)) * r0 + P(T_fix < inf) * rn' with exponents i, M_0, M_T, 0, n and no minus sign [sign slip in the source: r^{-i} = E[r^{-M_0}] = ... r^{-n} is meant; the rearranged result (4) is consistent with the minus signs]. p. 7, Theorem 2.1: the printed denominator is '1 - 1/r' where eq. (4) and Theorem 3.1 (p. 9) have '1 - 1/r^n'.

ku_moran58.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, arXiv:2403.12598v2, p. 18 (reference list) and p. 2
ku_moran58.text: [Mor58] P. A. P. Moran. 'Random processes in genetics'. In: Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 54 (1958), pp. 60-71. [p. 18]. ... the classic Moran Process ... was introduced in 1958, see [Mor58]. [p. 2]. (Moran 1958 itself was not read.)

marion_markov.source: E. Marion, A Formalization of the Ionescu-Tulcea Theorem in Mathlib, arXiv:2506.18616v5 [math.PR], 17 Mar 2026, p. 5 and p. 12
marion_markov.text: Likewise if we take X_n = X and kappa_n = kappa : X ~> X for all n we get a Markov kernel from X to X_{>=1} which, if we compose it with a measure mu at the beginning, gives the measure associated to a Markov chain with initial distribution mu and transition kernel kappa. [p. 5]. ... def traj (a : N) : Kernel (Pi i : Iic a, X i) (Pi n, X n) [p. 12]. 'The code is now fully integrated to Mathlib and is therefore available to anybody who wishes to do formalization using Lean.' [p. 1]

lagatta_price.source: T. LaGatta, The Mathematics of Evolution: The Price Equation, Natural Selection, and Environmental Change, arXiv:2202.10289v4 [math.PR], 4 Dec 2022, p. 9 (Section 1.3)
lagatta_price.text: The Price equation states that the average change is the sum of selective change and environmental change, with no additional components: Delta(X-bar) = d_NS(X) + d_EC(X) = cov(X, U) + E[Delta_w(X) U]. (1.6) ... Fisher's fundamental theorem [Pri72a] states that the selective change of relative fitness is equal to its variance: d_NS(U) = cov(U, U) = var(U). (1.8)  [U = W/W-bar is relative fitness.]

lagatta_agg.source: T. LaGatta, arXiv:2202.10289v4, p. 18 (Section 2.4, eq. (2.24)) and p. 19 (eq. (2.27))
lagatta_agg.text: The aggregate version states that selective change of fitness is proportional to its variance: d_NS(W) = cov(W, U) = var(W)/W-bar. (2.24) [p. 18]. ... When we apply this to the full fitness functions, we have: W'-bar - W-bar = d_NS(W) + d_EC(W, W') = var(W)/W-bar + E[Delta_w(W, W') W]/W-bar. (2.27) [p. 19]

lagatta_price72.text: In Price's view, 'The main cause of misunderstanding about the theorem is that everyone has supposed that Fisher was talking about the total change rather than just the fraction of this due to natural selection' [Pri72a, p. 130].

lagatta_refs.text: [Pri70] George R Price. Selection and covariance. Nature, 227:520-21, 1970. ... [Pri72a] George R Price. Fisher's 'fundamental theorem' made clear. Annals of human genetics, 36(2):129-140, a 1972. (The originals were not read.)

baez_const.source: J. C. Baez, The Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection, arXiv:2107.05610v3 [q-bio.PE], 6 Oct 2021, p. 4 (Section 2)
baez_const.text: The second term of equation (5) only vanishes in special cases, e.g. when the fitness functions f_i are constant. When the second term vanishes we have d f-bar/dt = Var(f). This is a satisfying result. It says the mean fitness does not decrease, and it increases whenever some replicators are more fit than others, at a rate equal to the variance in fitness.

baez_ewens.source: J. C. Baez, arXiv:2107.05610v3, p. 1 and p. 2
baez_ewens.text: Some tried to make this statement precise as follows: The time derivative of the mean fitness of a population equals the variance of its fitness. But this is only true under very restrictive conditions, so a controversy was ignited. [p. 1]. ... Ewens concluded that 'the theorem does not provide the substantial biological statement that Fisher claimed'. [p. 2]
